condition: Haemorrhoidal outlet bleeding in a young adult
summary: 24-year-old woman with three months of intermittent bright red blood on the paper after hard stools; no change in bowel habit, weight loss or anaemia; grade I haemorrhoids on proctoscopy. Outpatient management; no suspected-cancer pathway and no resuscitation.

inputs.hpi: Three months of intermittent bright red blood on the toilet paper and dripping into the pan after passing hard stools, 1–2 times a week. Painless. No change in bowel habit, no mucus, no weight loss, no abdominal pain. No family history of bowel cancer or IBD. Diet low in fibre.

exam.other: PR: normal, no mass, no blood. Proctoscopy: grade I internal haemorrhoids, no fissure.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: First-degree internal haemorrhoids
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Grade I internal haemorrhoids with outlet-type bleeding. No red-flag features.

emergencyLevel.note: Outlet-type bleeding at 24 with no other features does not meet NG12 referral criteria; it is not an emergency.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web adaptiveTriage has no negation handling and treats any "bleed/bleeding" as an urgent red flag (RED_FLAGS "GI or other bleeding" → emergency_now), so every rectal bleed — including minor outlet bleeding — is "emergency".

mustInclude.note: ASCRS 2024: dietary fibre is first-line for symptomatic haemorrhoids.

mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web computeClinicalPrompts fires the "GI haemorrhage" resuscitation prompt (2 large-bore cannulae, Hartmann’s bolus, cross-match 2 units) for any rectal-bleeding chip, regardless of volume, haemodynamics or Hb.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: rectal bleeding under 50 → consider referral only with abdominal pain, change in bowel habit, weight loss or iron-deficiency anaemia
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — management of hemorrhoids
guideline.section: Dietary fibre first-line; office procedures for grade I–III
guideline.citation: Hawkins AT, Davis BR, Bhama AR, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of hemorrhoids. Dis Colon Rectum. 2024;67:614–623.

guideline.name: BSG guideline — diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Minor outlet bleeding is managed as an outpatient
guideline.citation: Oakland K, Chadwick G, East JE, et al. Diagnosis and management of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding: guidelines from the British Society of Gastroenterology. Gut. 2019;68:776–789.

rationale: Pairs with crc-cibh-fit-positive-older (older patient with change in bowel habit): same symptom chip, opposite management. Tests over-triage of benign outlet bleeding (every "bleed" is scored as an emergency on web) and whether the suspected-cancer pathway is kept for the patients who meet it.
